title: Technical English — Course 5, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 5

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the revision-control briefing take place?
tasks.audioText: The engineering documentation manager will explain revision control on Friday at nine forty-five. Students should meet in the project room and bring the sample document register. The briefing will show how revision letters, dates and approval status are recorded. Students will compare two versions and identify which one is marked as current and approved.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which register should students bring?
tasks.audioText: The engineering documentation manager will explain revision control on Friday at nine forty-five. Students should meet in the project room and bring the sample document register. The briefing will show how revision letters, dates and approval status are recorded. Students will compare two versions and identify which one is marked as current and approved.

tasks.prompt: Revision control helps users identify the current approved version of a technical document. A document register may record its identifier, revision, issue date and approval status. When a new revision is released, the organisation should manage obsolete copies so that they are not mistaken for current information. A clear change history also helps reviewers understand what has been updated. Reading 1. What information may a document register contain?
options: Document identifier, revision, issue date and approval status
Supplier name, delivery date, invoice number and price
Room number, course title, lesson date and student group
Author name, file size, print date and storage location

tasks.prompt: Why should obsolete copies be managed?
options: To make it easier to print older copies
To prevent them from being mistaken for current information
To avoid recording the document revision
To allow users to select whichever version is easiest to read

tasks.prompt: Obsolete copies ___ so that they are not used by mistake.
Choose TWO fields that help identify a controlled document.
A list that records controlled documents and their current versions is a document ___.
You find two versions of a maintenance document. What should you do?
options: Use the one with more pages.
Check the document register for the current approved revision.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of revision control in a logical order.
options: Confirm approval status in the register
Make sure obsolete copies are not used
Check its revision and issue date
correctOrder: Check its revision and issue date
Confirm approval status in the register
Make sure obsolete copies are not used

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining why revision control matters for technical documentation. Include identifiers, approval and obsolete copies.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total. Score each criterion 0–2: (1) Identification — 2: explains document number/title, revision and applicable configuration; 1: partial; 0: absent. (2) Approval and currency — 2: explains approval/effective status and checking the current controlled source; 1: partial; 0: absent. (3) Obsolete-copy control — 2: explains withdrawal or clear prevention of obsolete copies being used; 1: vague; 0: absent. (4) English — 2: clear organisation and accurate document-control vocabulary; 1: errors but meaning clear; 0: meaning frequently unclear.
